docs.title: Crypto Policy, Stablecoin Exposure, and Inflation
docs.text:
This project studies whether stablecoin-driven digital dollarization is associated with inflation outcomes across countries.

I construct a country-month panel using:

  • GDELT crypto policy news
  • Google Trends Bitcoin attention
  • CoinMetrics USDT market capitalization
  • IMF CPI inflation and exchange-rate data
  • World Bank and IMF macroeconomic controls

The project includes policy data construction, variable engineering, fixed-effect panel regressions, mechanism tests, and heterogeneity analysis across crypto policy regimes.

Read the full project documentation

docs.title: AI-Assisted Creation on Pure-Content UGC Platforms
docs.text: This project studies whether pure-content UGC platforms should introduce AI-assisted creation tools and how such tools affect creators' content quality decisions.

docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text:
Pure-content UGC platforms rely on creators to produce engaging content and attract consumer attention. With the development of generative AI, platforms can provide AI-assisted creation tools such as automatic subtitle generation, AI script writing, one-click editing, AI visual effects, AI avatars, and personalized voices.

This project develops analytical models to study a platform's decision to launch AI-assisted tools and choose the optimal assistance intensity. The model captures the trade-off between AI-driven efficiency and creativity improvements, increased content homogeneity, and platform development costs.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Working paper / draft manuscript.

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text: • Research involvement: May 2026 – August 2026

docs.title: Research Questions
docs.text:
• Under what conditions should a pure-content UGC platform launch AI-assisted creation tools?
  • How should the platform choose the optimal AI assistance intensity?
  • Do creators benefit from AI-assisted tools?
  • How does AI usage affect content quality, browsing volume, creator profit, platform profit, and consumer surplus?
  • How do creator characteristics, such as creativity and production efficiency, affect equilibrium outcomes?

docs.title: Methodology
docs.text:
The project develops a sequential game-theoretic model involving a UGC platform, a content creator, and consumers.

The decision sequence is:

  1. The platform decides whether to introduce AI-assisted creation tools and chooses the assistance intensity.
  2. The creator chooses the production level of content.
  3. Consumers decide their browsing volume.

The analysis uses backward induction and comparative statics to characterize equilibrium outcomes. The model accounts for AI-driven production efficiency gains, creativity enhancement, content homogeneity, and development costs.

docs.title: Main Findings
docs.text:
• AI-assisted tools can improve content creativity and production efficiency, but they may also increase content homogeneity.
  • The platform should introduce AI tools when creator efficiency is low, AI-induced homogeneity is limited, or creators have strong creative ability.
  • The optimal AI assistance intensity is not necessarily the level that maximizes content quality, because the platform must balance quality improvement, homogeneity risk, and development cost.
  • When AI tools are introduced, content quality, consumer browsing volume, creator profit, and consumer surplus can increase under the model's adoption conditions.
  • The effect of creator efficiency is nuanced: after AI introduction, higher creator efficiency may not always improve creator profit or consumer surplus.
  • Creator creativity consistently improves content quality and benefits the platform, creators, and consumers.

docs.title: Extensions
docs.text:
The project further examines:

  • Different consumer weights on creativity and production quality.
  • Creator competition on the platform.
  • Endogenous platform subsidies to creators.
  • AI technical defects and their impact on platform and creator decisions.

docs.title: Crypto Policy, Stablecoin Exposure, and Inflation
Project Overview
docs.text:
This project studies whether stablecoin exposure is associated with inflation outcomes across countries.

The core idea is to combine local crypto attention with a global stablecoin expansion shock. Countries with higher Bitcoin search attention are treated as more exposed to global USDT market-cap growth.

docs.title: Research Question
docs.text:
Does stablecoin-driven digital dollarization affect inflation?

More specifically, this project asks:

  • Whether lagged stablecoin exposure is associated with year-over-year CPI inflation.
  • Whether crypto policy intensity changes the relationship.
  • Whether the effect differs across Legal, Restricted, and Illegal crypto policy regimes.
  • Whether exchange-rate and macro-financial channels help explain the relationship.

docs.title: Data Sources
docs.text: Component Source Role Crypto policy news GDELT 2.0 GKG titles Construct policy attention and restrictiveness Local crypto attention Google Trends Bitcoin search index Measure country-level crypto attention Stablecoin shock CoinMetrics USDT market capitalization Measure global stablecoin expansion Inflation IMF CPI data Main dependent variable Exchange rate IMF exchange-rate data Exchange-rate channel Macro controls World Bank / IMF Fiscal, monetary, unemployment, and current-account controls

docs.title: Key Variable Construction
docs.text:
The main exposure variable is:

$$ StablecoinExposure_{i,t} = BitcoinAttentionScaled_{i,t} \times USDTGrowthShock_t $$

where:

  • BitcoinAttentionScaled is Google Trends Bitcoin attention divided by 100.
  • USDTGrowthShock is the monthly log growth of USDT market capitalization.
  • The lagged version is used in the main regressions to reduce contemporaneous reverse-causality concerns.

docs.title: Policy Variables
docs.text:
From GDELT title-level crypto policy news, I construct country-month policy variables:

Variable Meaning Policy news attention log(1 + number of unique crypto policy titles) Average policy restrictiveness Average tone of policy-related titles Restrictive policy dummy Whether at least one restrictive policy title appears Policy restriction intensity Average restrictiveness × policy news attention

docs.title: Empirical Strategy
docs.text:
The preferred model estimates year-over-year CPI inflation as a function of lagged standardized stablecoin exposure, policy restriction intensity, macroeconomic controls, mechanism interactions, and fixed effects.

The specification includes:

  • Country fixed effects
  • Year fixed effects
  • Calendar-month fixed effects
  • Lagged macro controls
  • Exchange-rate and external vulnerability interactions

docs.title: Main Results
docs.text:
The preferred final model finds a statistically significant negative association between lagged standardized stablecoin exposure and year-over-year CPI inflation.

The all-mechanism robustness model keeps the stablecoin exposure coefficient negative and significant, while adding the fiscal deficit × broad money growth interaction.

docs.title: Policy Regime Heterogeneity
docs.text:
I classify countries into three crypto policy regimes:

  • Legal
  • Restricted
  • Illegal

The regime interaction results suggest that the negative stablecoin exposure effect is mainly concentrated in Restricted countries.

docs.title: Demo Code: Stablecoin Exposure Construction
docs.text:
import numpy as np

# Scale Google Trends Bitcoin attention to a 0-1 range
panel["bitcoin_attention_scaled"] = panel["bitcoin_attention"] / 100

# Construct global USDT growth shock
panel["log_usdt_marketcap"] = np.log(panel["usdt_marketcap"])
panel["usdt_growth_shock"] = panel["log_usdt_marketcap"].diff()

# Construct country-month stablecoin exposure
panel["stablecoin_exposure"] = (
    panel["bitcoin_attention_scaled"] * panel["usdt_growth_shock"]
)

# Use lagged exposure in regressions
panel["stablecoin_exposure_l1"] = (
    panel.groupby("country")["stablecoin_exposure"].shift(1)
)

docs.title: Demo Code: Fixed-Effect Regression
docs.text:
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

formula = """
inflation_yoy ~
    stablecoin_exposure_l1_z
    + policy_restriction_intensity_l1_z
    + dlog_exchange_rate_eop_l1_z
    + fiscal_deficit_pct_gdp_l1_z
    + unemployment_rate_l1_z
    + current_account_deficit_pct_gdp_l1_z
    + broad_money_growth_l1_z
    + crypto_x_fx_z
    + fx_x_ca_deficit_z
    + C(country)
    + C(year)
    + C(calendar_month)
"""

model = smf.ols(formula=formula, data=panel_reg).fit(cov_type="HC3")

print(model.summary())

docs.title: Pay-on-Delivery and Distribution Contracts
docs.text: This project studies how pay-on-delivery services affect distribution contract choices on e-commerce platforms.

docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text:
Pay-on-delivery allows consumers to postpone payment until product receipt. This service can reduce the disadvantage of online channels caused by delivery delay, but it may also create cash-flow opportunity costs for firms.

This project develops a game-theoretic model of a dual-channel supply chain, where a manufacturer sells through an offline channel and also cooperates with an e-commerce platform online. The online channel can operate under either a wholesale contract or an agency contract. The project studies when pay-on-delivery should be adopted and how it changes the manufacturer's distribution-contract choice.

docs.title: Manuscript
docs.text:
A draft manuscript for this project is available below.

Download PDF

docs.title: Research Questions
docs.text:
• When should an e-commerce platform offer pay-on-delivery?
  • When should a manufacturer adopt pay-on-delivery under an agency contract?
  • How does pay-on-delivery affect online and offline channel demand?
  • How does pay-on-delivery change the manufacturer's choice between wholesale and agency contracts?
  • What are the implications for firm profits, consumer surplus, and social welfare?

docs.title: Methodology
docs.text:
The project uses analytical game-theoretic models to compare different channel structures and payment schemes. The model considers four main scenarios:

  1. Wholesale contract without pay-on-delivery.
  2. Wholesale contract with pay-on-delivery.
  3. Agency contract without pay-on-delivery.
  4. Agency contract with pay-on-delivery.

The analysis uses backward induction to derive equilibrium pricing, demand, profit, consumer surplus, and social welfare outcomes.

docs.title: Main Findings
docs.text:
• Pay-on-delivery can mitigate the online channel's disadvantage caused by delivery delay.
  • Under a wholesale contract, the platform may offer pay-on-delivery when the consumer benefit from delayed payment outweighs the firm's cash-flow opportunity cost.
  • Under an agency contract, adoption is more restrictive because the manufacturer directly bears delayed revenue realization and service-related costs.
  • Pay-on-delivery can reshape the manufacturer's preference between wholesale and agency contracts.
  • The service may reduce consumer surplus in some cases, but it can improve social welfare within the model.

docs.title: Extensions
docs.text:
The project also considers two extensions:

  • Product returns in the online channel.
  • Different discount factors for product valuation and cash payment.

These extensions show that the main mechanism remains robust when additional operational features are introduced.

docs.title: Dynamic Control on UGC Platforms
docs.text: This project studies how user-generated content platforms should dynamically balance pure content quality and recommendation intensity when consumer reference-quality effects are present.

docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text:
User-generated content platforms increasingly rely on a mixed content ecosystem, where pure content attracts and retains users, while shoppable content generates commercial revenue. This project develops a dynamic analytical model to study how a UGC platform and a content creator make strategic decisions over time.

The model focuses on the interaction between pure content quality, platform recommendation intensity, user engagement, and consumer reference quality. It compares static decisions, dynamic decisions without uncertainty, and dynamic decisions with stochastic reference-quality uncertainty.

docs.title: Paper
docs.text:
This project has been published in the Journal of the Operational Research Society.

Download PDF

docs.title: Research Questions
docs.text:
• How should a UGC platform determine the recommendation intensity of pure content?
  • How should a content creator adjust pure content quality over time?
  • How does consumer reference quality affect user engagement and platform profitability?
  • How does uncertainty in reference quality change the strategies of platforms and creators?

docs.title: Methodology
docs.text:
The project uses game-theoretic modeling, optimal control theory, and differential games. It analyzes three scenarios:

  1. Static pure content quality and recommendation intensity.
  2. Dynamic quality and recommendation intensity without reference-quality uncertainty.
  3. Dynamic decision-making with stochastic reference-quality uncertainty.

Numerical simulations are used to illustrate the optimal paths of reference quality, content quality, recommendation intensity, user engagement, and profit outcomes.

docs.title: Main Findings
docs.text:
• Dynamic strategies can increase UGC platform profits compared with static decisions.
  • Dynamic decision-making may reduce content creators' earnings relative to a static environment.
  • Higher uncertainty in reference quality may reduce platform profits but create opportunities for content creators.
  • When reference-quality uncertainty is higher, the platform should increase pure-content recommendation intensity, while creators may reduce content quality.

  • Assisted with numerical analysis and simulation-based comparison across scenarios.
  • Helped organize the research logic and manuscript presentation.
  • Participated in the preparation of a co-authored journal paper.
